comments: A reports five of Spain's seven goals and ties its pressing/transition claims to named players; B never mentions a goal and describes Spain's final passes as frequently cut off, which badly misrepresents a 7-0.

A omits Henderson's and Kane's goals and wrongly calls Saka's goal the one that put England ahead; B has the correct goal sequence and adds the half-time Senegal change, though its tactical points are partly generic.
A gets the scoreline right and explains Australia's late switch to direct balls after the own goal; B describes similar patterns but leaves out every goal, so it misstates how the match unfolded.

A has richer tactical detail but omits both goals and suggests the defences cancelled each other out; B records the Maeda and Perisic goals and the shootout correctly, with reasonable though more generic tactical points.
Both describe Spain's sterile possession and Morocco's block and direct outlet; A has more event detail but never gives the result, while B correctly reports Morocco's shootout win and its scorers.
A leaves out all five goals and gives a misleading picture of a contested game; B states all goals correctly and links Brazil's early dominance to recoveries and transitions.

A misses three Portugal goals (including Ramos's hat-trick completion) but at least shows Portugal's dominance; B has no goals and presents Switzerland as controlling the game, which contradicts a 6-1 result.

A correctly explains the Dutch switch to an aerial route with de Jong and Weghorst as the cause of the comeback; B omits all four goals, says the match stayed deadlocked, and wrongly has De Paul leaving after 37 minutes.
A omits Petkovic's equaliser and wrongly says Brazil held on; B gives the correct sequence, links Croatia's push forward to the equaliser, and covers the shootout.
Both identify Morocco's left-side play and Portugal's deep circulation, but A never mentions En-Nesyri's winning goal; B ties Morocco's aerial threat to the winning header.

A calls Alvarez's goal the opener, leaving out Messi's penalty and Alvarez's second, so its account is wrong despite good transition analysis; B has the first two goals right but omits the 68th-minute third, and its tactical points are thinner.

A reports all three goals and gives a plausible tactical story (Croatia's possession, then direct balls to Petkovic); B has no goals at all, so its account of Croatian control lacks the decisive events.
A covers five of six goals and France's second-half change but leaves out Mbappe's 118th-minute equaliser and the shootout; B has no goals and says Argentina held off France, which is wrong.
